metadata.title: Tree of Life — Video Reference & Scientific Species Inventory
metadata.projectScope: Phase 1 Continuation · Taxon Inventory & Phase 2 Expansion Planning

videoSourceNotice.statement: The five reference YouTube videos cited in the initial design brief were not provided with URLs, identifiers, or transcript files in the local workspace or environment. In accordance with Rule 3 ('Do not invent species names, timestamps, or claims about video contents'), Rule 5 ('Clearly mark uncertain identifications and inaccessible video content'), and SCIENTIFIC_DATA_POLICY Section 3 ('Zero Fabrication Policy'), timestamps are recorded as null and video streams are marked inaccessible, rather than fabricating video claims or artificial timestamps.

verificationSources: Weiss et al. (2016) Nature Microbiology: The physiology and habitat of the last universal common ancestor
Open Tree of Life Synth ID: ott805080
taxa.confidenceNotes: Inferred from universal molecular homologies across all cellular life (ribosomal core, 20 L-amino acids, ATP synthase). LUCA is strictly NOT the origin of life; it was preceded by prebiotic chemistry and early protocells.

verificationSources: WoRMS (World Register of Marine Species) AphiaID: 6
Dresser Formation microfossils (Pilbara Craton, Western Australia ~3.48 BYA)
taxa.confidenceNotes: Established primary biological domain verified by isotopic carbon fractionation and fossil stromatolite benthic layers.

verificationSources: LPSN (List of Prokaryotic names with Standing in Nomenclature)
taxa.confidenceNotes: Ancestral alphaproteobacteria gave rise to eukaryotic mitochondria via endosymbiosis.

verificationSources: Fischer et al. (2016) Science: The evolution of oxygenic photosynthesis
NASA Earth Observatory Phytoplankton & Microbial Bloomsday Records
taxa.confidenceNotes: Oxygenic photosynthesis evolved prior to the Great Oxidation Event (~2.45–2.22 BYA). Primary plastid ancestor of Archaeplastida.
Major division of Gram-positive bacteria, critical components of the mammalian gut microbiome and spore formers.

verificationSources: Woese & Fox (1977) PNAS: Phylogenetic structure of the prokaryotic domain: The primary kingdoms
taxa.confidenceNotes: Distinct prokaryotic domain characterized by ether-linked isoprenoid membrane lipids and eukaryotic-like transcription/translation machinery.

verificationSources: LPSN / Bergey's Manual of Systematic Archaea and Bacteria
taxa.confidenceNotes: Encompasses methanogens (methanogenesis is an ancient Archean metabolic pathway), extreme halophiles, and thermophiles.
Hyperthermophilic archaea predominantly colonizing volcanic solfataras and hydrothermal vents.

verificationSources: Spang et al. (2015) Nature: Complex archaea that bridge the gap between prokaryotes and eukaryotes
Rodrigues-Oliveira et al. (2023) Nature: Isolation of an Asgard archaeon (Lokiarchaeum ossiferum)
taxa.confidenceNotes: Revolutionary phylogenomic discovery verifying that Eukaryota branch from within the Asgard archaeal lineage (2-domain eocyte tree of life hypothesis).

imageRequirements.proposedSource: Nature Publishing / Rodrigues-Oliveira et al. (Electron micrograph)

verificationSources: Brocks et al. (1999) Science: Sterane chemical fossils and early eukaryote biomarkers
Franceville biota / Bangiomorpha pubescens microfossils (~1.6–1.05 BYA)
taxa.confidenceNotes: Eukaryogenesis originated through the endosymbiosis of an alphaproteobacterium (mitochondrion) inside an Asgard-related archaeal host.

verificationSources: Kenrick & Crane (1997) Nature: The origin and early evolution of plants on land
taxa.confidenceNotes: Embryophyte land plants diverged from streptophyte green algae in the Ordovician Period (~470 MYA).
Paraphyletic assemblage of aquatic photosynthetic eukaryotes from which embryophyte land plants originated.

verificationSources: Wellman et al. (2003) Nature: Fragments of the earliest land plants
taxa.confidenceNotes: Earliest divergent clade of terrestrial embryophytes, lacking lignified vascular xylem/phloem.
Seedless vascular plants reproducing via spores, radiating in Carboniferous coal-swamp forests.

verificationSources: Christenhusz et al. (2011) Phytotaxa: A new classification and linear sequence of extant gymnosperms
taxa.confidenceNotes: Non-flowering seed plants (conifers, cycads, ginkgoes) that dominated Mesozoic floras.

verificationSources: Darwin's 'abominable mystery' regarding Cretaceous angiosperm radiation
taxa.confidenceNotes: Clade of plants with enclosed seeds and flowers for insect/vertebrate biotic pollination.
Monocot family fueling Miocene open grassland expansions and human agricultural civilizations.

verificationSources: Ramírez et al. (2007) Nature: Fossil orchid in Dominican amber and late Cretaceous origin
taxa.confidenceNotes: Enormously diverse family (>28,000 species) exhibiting specialized bilateral pollinator co-evolution.

verificationSources: Loron et al. (2019) Nature: Early fungi from the Proterozoic of Arctic Canada
taxa.confidenceNotes: Opisthokont kingdom of heterotrophic eukaryotes possessing chitinous cell walls, more closely related to animals than to plants.
Major subkingdom Dikarya phylum producing sexually derived basidiospores on club-shaped basidia.
The largest fungal phylum, encompassing yeasts (Saccharomyces), filamentous molds, morels, and lichen-forming fungi.

verificationSources: Erwin et al. (2011) Science: The Cambrian conundrum: early divergence and later ecological success of early animals
taxa.confidenceNotes: Multicellular heterotrophic opisthokonts possessing blastular embryonic stages and extracellular collagen matrix.
Basal metazoans lacking true tissue differentiation and germ layers, filter-feeding through aquiferous choanocyte canals.
Diploblastic metazoans possessing radial symmetry and specialized stinging organelles (cnidocytes).

verificationSources: Bobrovskiy et al. (2018) Science: Ancient steroids establish the Ediacaran fossil Dickinsonia as one of the earliest animals
taxa.confidenceNotes: Biomarker cholesterol analysis confirmed animal affinity. Distinct quilt-like segmented morphology lacking bilateral guts.

verificationSources: Edgecombe & Legg (2014) Paleontological Society: Origins and early evolution of arthropods
taxa.confidenceNotes: Ecdysozoans with chitinous cuticular exoskeletons, jointed appendages, and compound eyes. Comprise over 80% of described living species.

verificationSources: Whittington & Briggs (1985) Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society: The largest Cambrian animal, Anomalocaris
Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History Burgess Shale Collection
taxa.confidenceNotes: Iconic Burgess Shale stem-arthropod apex predator possessing barbed raptorial frontal appendages and circular mouth cones.

verificationSources: Whittington (1975) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. B: The enigmatic animal Opabinia regalis
Royal Ontario Museum Burgess Shale Database
taxa.confidenceNotes: Famous 5-eyed stem-arthropod possessing a frontal flexible proboscis terminating in grasping claws.
Abundant Middle Cambrian ptychopariid trilobite from the Wheeler Shale of Utah; iconic 3-lobed calcified arthropod.

verificationSources: Misof et al. (2014) Science: Phylogenomics resolves the timing and pattern of insect evolution
taxa.confidenceNotes: Hexapod pancrustaceans with three tagmata (head, thorax, abdomen), first animals to evolve powered flight in the Carboniferous.
Chelicerate arthropods with two body regions and four pairs of walking legs, early terrestrial colonizers in the Silurian.

verificationSources: McKenna et al. (2019) PNAS: The evolution and genomic basis of beetle diversity
taxa.confidenceNotes: Hyper-diverse holometabolous order characterized by hardened forewings (elytra) protecting membraneous hindwings.

verificationSources: Kawahara et al. (2019) PNAS: Phylogenomics reveals the timing and pattern of butterfly evolution
taxa.confidenceNotes: Co-radiated extensively with Cretaceous and Paleogene angiosperm flowering plants.

verificationSources: Kocot et al. (2011) Nature: Phylogenomics reveals deep molluscan relationships
taxa.confidenceNotes: Lophotrochozoan protostomes with a mantle, radula, and muscular foot; extraordinary range from bivalves to cephalopods.
Deuterostomes defined by a notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, and endostyle.

verificationSources: Shu et al. (1999) Nature: Lower Cambrian vertebrates from south China
taxa.confidenceNotes: Chordates with a cranium, neural crest cells, and cartilaginous or bony vertebral column replacing the notochord.
Paraphyletic grade representing non-tetrapod aquatic gill-bearing craniates.

verificationSources: Anderson & Westneat (2007) Biology Letters: Feeding mechanics and bite force of the arthrodire Dunkleosteus
Cleveland Museum of Natural History Placoderm Specimen CMNH 5768
taxa.confidenceNotes: Giant Late Devonian arthrodire placoderm apex predator with self-sharpening gnathal plates delivering one of the highest bite forces in history.
Cartilaginous jawed vertebrates possessing placoid denticles and electrosensory ampullae of Lorenzini.

verificationSources: Betancur-R et al. (2017) BMC Evolutionary Biology: Phylogenetic classification of bony fishes
taxa.confidenceNotes: Dominant vertebrate class (>33,000 species) possessing lepidotrichia (fin rays) and swim bladders.

verificationSources: Daeschler, Shubin, & Jenkins (2006) Nature: A Devonian tetrapod-like fish and the evolution of the tetrapod body plan
Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University Specimen NUFV 108
taxa.confidenceNotes: Morphological milestone transitional fossil bridging elpistostegalian fish and earliest limbed tetrapods: possesses wrists, flat skull, neck, and ribs.

imageRequirements.attributionRequired: Zina Deretsky / National Science Foundation (Artistic reconstruction)

taxa.confidenceNotes: Anamniotic tetrapods characterized by moist, permeable skin and biphasic aquatic larval / terrestrial adult life cycles.

verificationSources: Frost, Darrel R. (2021) Amphibian Species of the World (AMNH)
taxa.confidenceNotes: Tailless lissamphibians specialized for saltatory jumping locomotion, auditory vocalization, and external amplexus fertilization.
Tailed lissamphibians with remarkable tissue regeneration capacity and paedomorphic forms (e.g. Ambystoma mexicanum).
Amniote clade encompassing squamates, turtles, crocodilians, and dinosaurs (including living birds).

verificationSources: Romer & Price (1940) Review of the Pelycosauria
Field Museum of Natural History Synapsid Collection
taxa.confidenceNotes: Permian sphenacodontid non-mammalian synapsid (stem-mammal). Strictly NOT a dinosaur; more closely related to mammals than reptiles.

verificationSources: Brusatte et al. (2015) Biological Reviews: The extinction of the dinosaurs
taxa.confidenceNotes: Dominant terrestrial archosaurs from the Late Triassic to Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction (Chicxulub bolide impact). Birds are the sole surviving avian lineage.

verificationSources: Osborn, H.F. (1905) Tyrannosaurus and other Cretaceous carnivorous dinosaurs (AMNH)
taxa.confidenceNotes: Apex coelurosaurian theropod of Late Cretaceous Laramidia; stratigraphically dated from Hell Creek and Lance formations.

verificationSources: Marsh, O.C. (1889) Notice of gigantic horned Dinosauria from the Cretaceous
taxa.confidenceNotes: Iconic chasmosaurine ceratopsid herbivore featuring a massive three-horned skull and parietosquamosal frill.

verificationSources: von Meyer, H. (1861) Archaeopteryx lithographica (Solnhofen limestone)
Natural History Museum London Specimen NHMUK PV OR 37001
Museum für Naturkunde Berlin Specimen HMN 1880
taxa.confidenceNotes: Pivotal transitional fossil displaying theropod skeletal traits (toothed jaws, clawed fingers, long bony tail) combined with flight feathers.

imageRequirements.proposedSource: Wikimedia Commons / Museum für Naturkunde Berlin
imageRequirements.authorCredit: H. v. Meyer / Museum für Naturkunde
imageRequirements.attributionRequired: Berlin Specimen / Museum für Naturkunde / Public Domain

taxa.confidenceNotes: Lepidosaurian reptiles characterized by cranial kinesis and horny epidermal scales; over 10,000 extant species.
Archelosaurian reptiles with bony carapace and plastron derived from fused ribs and vertebrae.
Extant pseudosuchian archosaurs, surviving sister group to birds (Aves).

verificationSources: Prum et al. (2015) Nature: A comprehensive phylogeny of modern birds
taxa.confidenceNotes: Living theropod maniraptoran dinosaurs that survived the K-Pg extinction event.

verificationSources: Oliveros et al. (2019) PNAS: Earth history and the passerine superradiation
taxa.confidenceNotes: Comprises more than 60% of all living avian species, possessing anisodactyl perching feet and complex syringeal song muscles.

verificationSources: Jarvis et al. (2014) Science: Whole-genome analyses resolve early branches in the tree of life of modern birds
taxa.confidenceNotes: Informal functional grouping representing diurnal predatory raptors with hooked beaks and sharp talons.

verificationSources: Vegaavis iaai K-Pg boundary fossil (Clarke et al. 2005, Nature)
taxa.confidenceNotes: Galloanserae clade of aquatic birds, among the earliest diverging modern neognath bird lineages.

verificationSources: Wilson & Reeder's Mammal Species of the World (MSW3)
Luo, Z.X. (2007) Nature: Transformation and diversification in early mammal evolution
taxa.confidenceNotes: Synapsid crown clade characterized by mammary glands, hair, neocortex, and three auditory middle ear ossicles.

verificationSources: Warren et al. (2008) Nature: Genome analysis of the platypus Ornithorhynchus anatinus
taxa.confidenceNotes: Basal living mammalian lineage of Australasian egg-laying prototherians.

verificationSources: Nilsson et al. (2010) PLoS Biology: Tracking the evolution of marsupials using retroposons
taxa.confidenceNotes: Endemic Australasian and Ameridelphian mammals rearing undeveloped altricial neonates within maternal pouches.

verificationSources: O'Leary et al. (2013) Science: The placental mammal ancestor and the post-K-Pg radiation
taxa.confidenceNotes: Crown clade characterized by prolonged intrauterine gestation supported by a chorioallantoic placenta.

verificationSources: Palkopoulou et al. (2015) Current Biology: Complete genomes reveal signatures of serious inbreeding in the last woolly mammoths
taxa.confidenceNotes: Pleistocene proboscidean megafauna adapted to Mammoth Steppe environments; survived on Wrangel Island until ~4,000 years ago.

verificationSources: La Brea Tar Pits & Museum Holotype Collection
Christiansen & Harris (2005) Journal of Morphology: Body size of Smilodon
taxa.confidenceNotes: Machairodontine felid megafaunal apex predator of the Pleistocene Americas; renowned for hyper-elongated maxillary canine teeth.

imageRequirements.proposedSource: Wikimedia Commons / La Brea Tar Pits
imageRequirements.attributionRequired: Charles R. Knight (Paleoart Reconstruction) / Public Domain

verificationSources: Groves, C.P. (2005) Mammal Species of the World: A Taxonomic and Geographic Reference
taxa.confidenceNotes: Euarchontoglires placental mammals characterized by enlarged cerebral cortices, stereoscopic forward-facing orbits, and grasping hands with nails.

verificationSources: Prado-Martinez et al. (2013) Nature: Great ape genetic diversity and population history
taxa.confidenceNotes: Catarrhine hominoids including orangutans (Pongo), gorillas (Gorilla), chimpanzees and bonobos (Pan), and humans (Homo).

verificationSources: Brunet et al. (2002) Nature: A new hominid from the Upper Miocene of Chad, Central Africa
Smithsonian Human Origins Program Sahelanthropus Specimen (TM 266-01-060-1, 'Toumaï')
taxa.confidenceNotes: One of the oldest known hominin candidates near the human-chimpanzee divergence; anterior position of the foramen magnum indicates habitual bipedal posture.

imageRequirements.proposedSource: Smithsonian Human Origins / Mission Paléoanthropologique Franco-Tchadienne

verificationSources: Johanson et al. (1978) Kirtlandia: A new species of the genus Australopithecus
Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History AL 288-1 ('Lucy')
taxa.confidenceNotes: Extensively documented Pliocene bipedal hominin possessing valgus knee angle and human-like pelvis combined with apelike cranial capacity (~380–500 cm³).
First archaic hominin with modern body proportions, expanded cranial capacity (~900–1100 cm³), systematic Acheulean bifacial handaxe technology, and migration out of Africa.

verificationSources: Green et al. (2010) Science: A draft sequence of the Neandertal genome
Smithsonian Human Origins Program (Feldhofer 1, Shanidar, La Chapelle-aux-Saints)
taxa.confidenceNotes: Eurasian Pleistocene hominin; genomic sequencing verified fertile interbreeding with non-African Homo sapiens (~1–2% introgressed DNA in modern non-African genomes).

verificationSources: Hublin et al. (2017) Nature: New fossils from Jebel Irhoud, Morocco and the pan-African origin of Homo sapiens
Smithsonian Human Origins Program Species Database
taxa.confidenceNotes: Anatomically modern humans — an extant terminal branch of hominine catarrhine primates. Strictly NOT an 'apex' or 'goal' of evolution.

imageRequirements.attributionRequired: Chip Clark / Smithsonian Human Origins Program

verificationSources: Flynn et al. (2005) Systematic Biology: Molecular phylogeny of the Carnivora
taxa.confidenceNotes: Laurasiatherian placental mammals characterized by specialized shearing carnassial teeth (P4/M1).

verificationSources: Johnson et al. (2006) Science: The Late Miocene radiation of modern Felidae
taxa.confidenceNotes: Feliform carnivorans specialized as obligate carnivores with protractile claws and hypercarnivorous dentition.
Pantherine cats capable of roaring due to an incompletely ossified hyoid apparatus.
Largest living felid species, apex solitary forest predator across Asia.
Only social felid living in stable matrilineal prides, sexually dimorphic maned males.

verificationSources: Lindblad-Toh et al. (2005) Nature: Genome sequence, comparative analysis and haplotype structure of the domestic dog
taxa.confidenceNotes: Caniform carnivorans adapted to cursorial pursuit predation and complex cooperative pack behavior.

verificationSources: Krause et al. (2008) BMC Evolutionary Biology: Mitochondrial genomes reveal an explosive radiation of extinct and extant bears
taxa.confidenceNotes: Caniform carnivorans with plantigrade locomotion and opportunistic omnivorous or herbivorous adaptations.

verificationSources: Thewissen et al. (2007) Nature: Whales originated from aquatic artiodactyls in the Eocene of India
taxa.confidenceNotes: Fully aquatic mammals cladistically nested within Artiodactyla (hippopotamus sister group).

verificationSources: Price et al. (2005) Biological Reviews: A complete phylogeny of the whales, dolphins and even-toed ungulates
taxa.confidenceNotes: Paraxonic ungulates bearing weight equally on the third and fourth digits, many featuring multi-chambered ruminant stomachs.

verificationSources: Fabre et al. (2012) BMC Evolutionary Biology: A glimpse on the pattern of rodent diversification
taxa.confidenceNotes: The single most species-rich mammalian order (~40% of all mammals), characterized by a single pair of continuously growing incisors.

verificationSources: Teeling et al. (2005) Science: A molecular phylogeny for bats illuminates biogeography and the fossil record
taxa.confidenceNotes: Only mammals with powered wing flight, utilizing ultrasonic laryngeal echolocation for nocturnal navigation and prey capture.
